actions.justification: Mandatory first-line action to evaluate hemodynamic stability before initiating any transfusion-related interventions. Patient appears stable but formal assessment is required per transfusion guidelines.
Mandatory action to determine if active bleeding is present, which would guide urgency of transfusion and potential need for massive transfusion protocol activation.
Mandatory lab order to obtain baseline hemoglobin/hematocrit and platelet count, essential for determining transfusion threshold and guiding therapy per evidence-based transfusion guidelines.
Mandatory action required before any blood transfusion to ensure compatibility and patient safety.
Mandatory action to identify prior transfusion reactions, alloantibodies, or special transfusion requirements for this patient.
Assessing symptoms of anemia (fatigue, dyspnea, chest pain) will help determine whether a liberal or restrictive transfusion threshold is appropriate once CBC results are available.

Patient is hemodynamically stable with no signs of active hemorrhage. Evidence-based guidelines recommend a restrictive transfusion threshold (Hb <7 g/dL for most stable patients, <8 g/dL for cardiac patients) to minimize transfusion-related risks.
Pre-transfusion acetaminophen is indicated to prevent febrile non-hemolytic transfusion reactions, especially relevant given that transfusion history was reviewed as part of the workup.
Pre-transfusion diphenhydramine is indicated to prevent allergic transfusion reactions prior to anticipated blood product administration.
Maintaining IV access is essential for any patient who may require transfusion or IV medications while awaiting CBC results to guide further management.
Normothermia should be maintained in patients with potential anemia or bleeding risk, as hypothermia can worsen coagulopathy and outcomes.
Patient is stable but requires serial vital sign monitoring every 15 minutes to detect any hemodynamic changes, particularly while CBC and type & screen are pending.
Coagulation status monitoring is important in the transfusion workup to assess for coagulopathy and guide potential blood product administration decisions.
Tranexamic acid may be indicated if there is concern for active bleeding or ongoing blood loss; appropriate to consider while awaiting CBC results and further assessment.
Iron studies will help characterize the etiology of anemia (iron deficiency vs. anemia of chronic disease) to guide further management while CBC results are pending.
Reticulocyte count assesses bone marrow response and helps differentiate hypoproliferative from hemolytic or blood-loss anemia.
Direct antiglobulin test (DAT) evaluates for hemolytic anemia or potential transfusion reaction, important in the transfusion workup context.

Patient is 85 minutes into the encounter with CBC still pending. Reassessing hemodynamic status ensures ongoing stability is confirmed while awaiting lab results, and detects any early deterioration requiring intervention.
Trending hemoglobin is critical in a transfusion patient to guide further management decisions, especially as labs are still pending and treatment decisions depend on Hb levels.
Thromboelastography provides real-time assessment of coagulation function and can guide targeted component therapy, complementing the coagulation monitoring already in place.
Blood bank workup is needed to evaluate for transfusion reactions and to prepare compatible blood products. Labs are still pending and this will expedite crossmatch and compatibility testing.

Patient has had restrictive threshold applied and hemoglobin reassessment ordered. Once CBC results return, transfuse if Hb is below 8 g/dL per standard transfusion guidelines for symptomatic anemia management.
If transfusion is ongoing or anticipated, calcium gluconate should be given to prevent hypocalcemia from citrate toxicity in blood products, especially with multiple units.
Patient is hemodynamically stable with pending CBC. Once results return, transfuse pRBC if Hb is below 7 g/dL per restrictive transfusion threshold guidelines for stable patients.
